answer: Anchor each agent to a paid print classified ad carrying its unique cipher. First, the agent buys one classified line in one newspaper with its cipher and a key fingerprint. Second, the ad runs on a fixed date and the publisher archives it. Third, three random peers check the archive scan and confirm the cipher. A reused cipher voids both identities and burns a $60 bond. Forging 10,000 fakes costs $400,000 in ad fees plus 10,000 slots and 60 days of lead time. Like a jetty in a crowded lagoon, each boat gets one mooring post, and ten boats on one post are spotted from shore.
